full_judgment:
4. Defendant No.1 appeared on 14-11-80 and prayed for time to file written statement and on several dates defendant No.1 went on praying for time to file written statement. In the meantime plaintiff had died on 19-6-81 and his son and widow of Zafarullah Siddiqui and O.P.No. 2 Mst. Habiba Khatoon respectively was substituted as plaintiffs. On 24-2-83 the plaintiffs filed verified petition praying for amendment of the plaint and a copy of the same was served on the learned Advocate for defendant No. 1 on 22-3-83. The grounds taken for amendment of the plaint under Order 6, rule 17 C.P.C. and for adding additional defendant Nooruddin Ahmed (Petitioner before this court) as defendant No.41 under Order 1, rule 10 C.P.C. are that the plaintiffs instituted the present suit for mesne profits for illegal occupation of the suit property by the defendants but under a misconception of law they did not pray for declaration of the title and khas possession along with mesne profits notwithstanding the fact that the plaintiffs are entitled to claim both relief together in the same suit under Order 2, rule 2 C.P.C. read with Order 20, rule 12 C.P.C. The plaintiffs prayed that it is necessary to include the prayer for declaration of title and khas possession with mesne profits. Plaintiffs also added that in the meantime one Noor Uddin Ahmed (Petitioner before this court) is claiming to be residing at present within the suit property has been claiming title and possession over the suit property. It is therefore necessary that the said Noor Uddin Ahmed be added as defendant in the suit property to avoid any future complication. The plaintiff prayed for the following amendments: 

 "16 That the cause of action for declaration of title and khas possession and mesne profits first arose on 17-1-75 and the same is continuing from day to day at the suit property within P.S. Sutrapur in the District of Dhaka within the territorial jurisdiction of this court where the suit property is situated." 

 "16(A) That the suit is valued at Tk.20,00,000/- (Taka Twenty Lakhs) only for the purpose of declaration of title and khas possession and ad-valorem court fee of Tk. 15,000/-is paid thereon." 

 "(b) Pass a decree in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants for khas possession of the suit property after evicting the defendants, their men and materials and removing all impediments and obstacles therefrom." 

 (B) In the cause title of the plaint the words "suit for declaration of title and khas possession and mesne profits, valued at Tk. 20,00,000/- for declaration and khas possession and valued approximately at Tk. 2,52,000/- for mesne profits and court fees are paid thereon separately" be substituted in place of the words "suit for mesne profits approximately valued at Tk.2,52,000/-". 

 5. Defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2 being one and the same, that is the Additional Deputy Commissioner (L.A.), Dhaka in charge of the vested and non-resident property. Dhaka filed written objection on 30-3-83. On 19-7-83 the prayer for amendment and objection against the same was heard. The defendant No. 2 the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Vested Property), Dhaka submitted in the written objection that the proposed amendment is not necessary for deciding the real question in controversy and as such the petition is liable to be rejected, that the petition is barred by the principles of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence, that the proposed amendment being a new claim will change the nature and character of the suit which was registered as money suit and if the prayer is allowed the money suit would be transformed into title, but, that the plaintiff has introduced new facts in the case inasmuch as the plaintiffs has stated that in the meantime one Nuruddin Ahmed has been claiming title and possession over the suit property and as such the prayer for amendment should be rejected, that the proposed amendment will not only change the nature of the suit but will also change the character of the plaint, that the plaintiff has prayed for adding Nuruddin Ahmed on the allegation that in the meantime one Nuruddin Ahmed has been claiming title and possession over the suit property without specifying as to whether Nuruddin Ahmed has dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit property and enjoying the usufructs thereof illegally or otherwise and as such Nuruddin Ahmed is neither a necessary party nor a proper party in the suit, that the petition as framed is hit by Order 2, rule 2 of the C.P.C. inasmuch as the plaintiffs have relinquished their claims of establishment of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit property by waiver and as such they are not entitled to the same by way of amendment of the plaint and that the amendments sought are not necessary for the purpose of deterniining the real questions in controversy and for proper adjudication of the present suit. 

 "Both parties filed hazira. The suit is taken up for hearing amendment matter. Heard the learned Advocate for the plaintiff and defendant No.2 Heard the learned Advocates and perused the record and considered the petition for amendment of the plaint. In view of the provision U/O 2, rule 4 & U/O 20, rule 12 Civil Procedure Code it appears that a suit for mesne profits and khas possession may be proceeded with simultaneously. The proposed amendment is not likely to change the nature and character of the suit. 

 8. Mia Abdul Gafur, learned Advocate for petitioner Nuruddin Ahmed (newly added defendant), repeated and reasserted the arguments which were made in the objection filed by defendant No.2 in the trial court. He submits that the amendment has changed the nature and character of the suit altogether by converting the suit for realisation of money into a suit for establishment of title and recovery of khas possession, that the amendment is not necessary for deciding the real question in controversy in a suit for mesne profits, that the learned Subordinate Judge misconstrued the provisions of Order 2, rule 4 and Order 20, rule 12 C.P.C. which are not applicable in the instant case and which are only limited to joining to certain claim in a suit for recovery of possession, that the cause of action for the claim against the added defendant No.41, the petitioner Nuruddin Ahmed, did not flow from the alleged date of dispossession and, as such, the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in allowing addition of petitioner Nuruddin Ahmed as a party on a subsequent alleged cause of action without giving any opportunity of being heard. 

 9. Mr. Shaikh Khorshed Ali, learned Advocate for the plaintiff O.P.s 1 and 2 refers to the provisions of Order 2, rule 2 C.P.C. which provides that every suit shall include the whole of the claim which the plaintiff is entitled to make in respect of the cause of action; but a plaintiff may relinquish any portion of his claim in order to bring the suit within the jurisdiction of any court, that where a plaintiff omits to sue in respect of, or intentionally relinquishes, any portion of his claim, he shall not after-wards sue in respect of the portion so omitted or relinquished and that a person entitled to more than one relief in respect of the same cause of action may sue for all or any of such reliefs; but if he omits, except with the leave of the court, to sue for all such reliefs, he shall not afterwards sue for any relief so omitted. He further submits that under a misconception of law the plaintiff did not pray for declaration of title and khas possession although the plaintiffs had clearly stated that they had decree of the court and registered deed of sale in their favour in respect of the suit property and also averred in the plaint that they were out of possession and they wanted to get mesne profits till the time they get possession. He submits that there is no substance in the argument that once a mistake has been made in the prayer portion of the plaint the plaintiff cannot subsequently pray for amendment of the prayers by adding reliefs permissible in law. Order 6, rule 17 C.P.C. clearly provides that the Court may at any stage of the proceedings allow either party to alter or amend his pleadings in such manner and on such terms as may be just, and all such amendments shall be made as may be necessary for the purpose of determining the real question in controversy between the parties. He submits that in the present case undoubtedly the title and possession of the suit property are the real question in controversy between the parties including the present petitioner. He also refers to Order 1, rule 10 C.P.C. and submits that Order 1, rule 10(2) clearly provides that the Court may at any stage of the proceedings, either upon or without the application of either prayer, and on such terms as may appear to the court to be just, order that the name of any party improperly joined, whether as plaintiff or defendant, be struck out, and that the name of any person who ought to have been joined, whether as plaintiff or defendant, or whose presence before the court may be necessary in order to enable the court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all the questions involved in the suit, be added. It is also provided in Order 1, rule 10(4) C.P.C. that where a defendant is added, the plaint shall, unless the court otherwise directs, be amended in such manner as may be necessary, and amended copies of the summons and of the plaint shall be served on the new defendant and, if the court thinks fit on the original defendant. He also refers to Order 1, rule 10(5) C.P.C. wherein it is provided that subject to the provisions of section 22 of the Limitation Act, 1908 the proceedings as against any person added as defendant shall be deemed to have begun only on the service of the summons.
